prompt:
I need the front end for Cardloft. A shared workshop for hobbyists designing their own tabletop games with friends, holding the rulebook, card set and playtest notes that everyone edits and comments on.

Who's using it: Hollis Marchetti, a nurse who designs board games on her evenings off. She's co-designing a trading game with two old college friends in other cities, and a few local friends act as playtesters.

What they're doing right now: It's Sunday afternoon after Saturday's four-player playtest, which ran 40 minutes long because the 'Harbor' cards made the economy snowball. Hollis is rewriting card text for the ship cards. Her co-designer Jun is editing the market-price cards right now, and she doesn't want to overwrite him. A playtester, Sam, left eleven comments overnight but can only comment, not edit. Hollis wants to see what Jun changed since yesterday, answer Sam's notes, accept or reject Jun's suggested rewrite of rule 4.2, and leave the rulebook in a state they can print for next weekend.

What's in the system at this point: Game: 'Saltwind Exchange', version 0.7. 84 cards in 5 decks (Ships 18, Harbor 12, Market 24, Events 20, Contracts 10), each with name, cost, effect text, flavor text, deck, version number and last editor. Rulebook of 11 sections, about 4,300 words. People: Hollis (owner), Jun Park (co-designer, currently editing Market cards), Teodora Silva (co-designer, last seen 3 days ago), and playtesters Sam and Aditi (comment-only). 23 changes since the Saturday playtest, 11 open comments from Sam, and 1 suggested rewrite of rule 4.2 'Docking'. Playtest log: 6 sessions, with the most recent on Nov 14 lasting 2 h 10 min against a 90 min target.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
